Method of Attack: Wrapping original Petya ransomware to execute custom commands
Uses Petya's encryption but stores keys and handles payments via own servers
Modifies ransom note to remove Petya references
Targets unsecured RDP servers via brute-force attacks
Compromises servers and endpoints using Windows PsExec utility
Escalates access inside networks after initial compromise
Discoverer: Kaspersky researchers Fedor Sinitsyn and Anton Ivanov
Impacted Systems: Windows servers and endpoints vulnerable to PsExec and unsecured RDP
Attack Vector: Spam campaigns or exploit kit-based distribution (for original Petya binaries)
Brute-force attacks on unsecured RDP servers
Indicators of Compromise: Customized ransom note without Petya name or flashing red skull
SHA256 hashes detailed in Kaspersky's blog post
